n8f9ecc97336.s: Which of the following is NOT correct?
o: The Vilasa grant was issued before Vijayanagara was founded
The Bahmani kingdom arose before Vijayanagara was founded
The truce ceding Golconda came in 1364–65
n8f9ecc97336.x: Vijayanagara was founded in 1336 and the Bahmani kingdom only in 1347; the Vilasa grant (1330) came before both.

ne846146c47c.s: Among the Gajapati rulers, whose Andhra campaigns came first?
ne846146c47c.x: Kapilendra, the founder, campaigned first; Purushottama followed and Prataparudra came after him.

n1c1b564fc32.s: Markandeya Puranam was written in Telugu by Tikkana's disciple:
n1c1b564fc32.x: Marana, a disciple of Tikkana, wrote Markandeya Puranam; Baddena wrote Sumathi Satakam and Manchana Keyurabahu Charitra.

na93bf3fd20c.s: Which work is a Kshetra-mahatmya kavya?
na93bf3fd20c.x: Nrusimha Puranam is a Kshetra-mahatmya kavya; Dasakumara Charitra is a story kavya and Raghavapandaviyam a dvyarthi kavya.

n331db93d215.x: Jayapa Senani wrote Nritta Ratnavali along with Geeta and Vadya Ratnavali; Vidyanatha wrote Prataparudra Yashobhushanam.

nae0ab4c661b.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Telugu?
o: It has been a classical language of India since 2008
Telugu Language Day falls on 29 August
Telugu Language Day marks the birth anniversary of Gurajada Apparao
29 August is the birth anniversary of Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy
nae0ab4c661b.x: Telugu Language Day (29 August) marks Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy's birth anniversary, not Gurajada Apparao's.

new.s: The Kaluvacheru grant names how many Nayakas who backed Prolaya Nayaka?
new.x: The Kaluvacheru grant (1423) names 75 Nayakas who supported Prolaya Nayaka.

new.s: The Kaluvacheru grant of 1423 was issued by the Reddi queen:
new.x: The Kaluvacheru grant (1423) was issued by Reddi queen Anitalli; the Vilasa grant was Prolaya Nayaka's.

new.s: Which of the following chiefs took part in the liberation movement but did NOT lead it?
new.x: Koppula Prolaya Nayaka was one of the chiefs who took part; the confederacy was led by Musunuri Prolaya Nayaka.

new.s: After the fall of Warangal in 1323, the deputy of Malik Burhanuddin in Andhra was:
new.x: Andhra was placed under Malik Burhanuddin with Malik Maqbul as deputy.

new.s: Of Prataparudra's generals, how many survived the fall of Warangal?
new.x: Of Prataparudra's 75 generals only three survived: Prolaya Nayaka, Recherla Singama and Prolaya Vema Reddi.

new.s: Prolaya Nayaka of the Musunuri family was the son of:
new.x: Prolaya Nayaka was the son of Potinayaka; being childless he was succeeded by his cousin Kapaya.

new.s: Prolaya Nayaka, being childless, was succeeded by his:
new.x: Prolaya Nayaka was childless and was succeeded by his cousin Kapaya Nayaka.

new.s: Which inscription names 14 members of the Musunuri lineage, of whom only 3 ruled?
new.x: The Polavaram inscription names 14 members of the lineage, only 3 of whom ruled.

new.s: Under Kapaya Nayaka, his nephew Anapota Nayaka served as governor at:
new.x: Kapaya's nephew Anapota Nayaka was governor at Vengi.

new.s: Which one of the following titles was borne by Kapaya Nayaka?
new.x: Kapaya held Andhra Suratrana, Andhradesadhisvara and Katakachurakara; Kavirajamarga is not his title.

new.s: Who, among the following, later bore the title 'Andhra Suratrana' after Kapaya Nayaka?
new.x: Kapaya was the first Andhra Suratrana; Anavema Reddi later held the title.

new.s: In which year did Kapaya Nayaka lose Bhuvanagiri to the Bahmanis?
new.x: Kapaya lost Kaulas in 1350 and Bhuvanagiri in 1356; Golconda was ceded in 1364-65.

new.s: Kapaya Nayaka's son Vinayaka Deva was burnt alive by the Bahmani Sultan:
new.x: Muhammad Shah I had Kapaya's son Vinayaka Deva burnt alive in 1361/62.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Musunuri–Bahmani truce of 1364–65:
1. Kapaya ceded Golconda.
2. Kapaya paid 33 lakhs and a turquoise throne.
3. Bhuvanagiri became the boundary.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Golconda, 33 lakhs, the turquoise throne and elephants and horses were given, and Golconda became the boundary; Bhuvanagiri had been lost in 1356.

new.s: After the battle of Bhimavaram (1367–68), Musunuri Telangana passed to the:
new.x: Anapota Nayaka killed Kapaya at Bhimavaram, ending the Musunuri line; Telangana passed to the Velamas.

new.s: Singama Nayaka I, founder of the independent Recherla kingdom, was killed by:
new.x: Singama Nayaka I was killed by the Jallipalli chiefs, not at Bhimavaram.

new.s: Mada Nayaka, made ruler of Devarakonda, was the younger brother of:
new.x: Mada Nayaka, younger brother of Anavota (Anapota) Nayaka, was made ruler of Devarakonda.

new.s: Who succeeded Mada Nayaka as ruler of Devarakonda?
new.x: Mada Nayaka's son Pedda Vedagiri succeeded him at Devarakonda.

new.s: The Rachakonda fort is noted for which construction technique?
new.x: Rachakonda fort is built in cyclopean masonry without mortar.

new.s: Devarakonda fort of the Recherla kings is a:
new.x: Devarakonda is a 14th-century hilltop fort of the Recherla kings.

new.s: The Recherla Velamas were also known as:
new.x: The Recherla Velamas were also called Padmanayakas; Chaturthanvayas refers to the Kamma clan of the Musunuris.

new.s: At the battle of Jallipalli, Singama Nayaka fought the Jallipalli Kshatriyas, who were aided by the:
new.x: At Jallipalli, the Jallipalli Kshatriyas, aided by the Reddis, killed Singama.

new.s: After Kapaya Nayaka's decline, coastal Andhra was taken by the:
new.x: After Kapaya's decline, the Reddis took coastal Andhra and the Velamas took Musunuri Telangana.

new.s: After their victory at Dharanikota, the Velamas took which title?
new.x: After Dharanikota the Velamas took the titles Jagadabbaganda and Rayavesa Bhujanga.

new.s: Lingamanidu of Devarakonda sought help from which Gajapati prince?
new.x: Lingamanidu of Devarakonda sought help from Gajapati Hamvira.

new.s: The Velamas helped Annadevu take Vengi from:
new.x: The Velamas helped Annadevu take Vengi from Kataya Vema.

new.s: Bammera Potana dedicated his Bhagavatam to:
new.x: Potana refused Sarvajna Singama Nayaka II and dedicated his Bhagavatam to Lord Rama.

new.s: Rasarnava Sudhakara, composed by Singa Bhupala of Rachakonda, deals with:
new.x: Rasarnava Sudhakara is a work on Sanskrit dramaturgy and poetics; Sangeeta Sudhakaram deals with music.

new.s: The Velugoti branch of the Velamas ruled:
new.x: Velugoti = Venkatagiri; Ravu = Bobbili; Damerla = Sri Kalahasti.

new.s: Which Velama family ruled Bobbili?
new.x: The Ravu family ruled Bobbili.

new.s: Which of the following Velama family–region pairs is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Ravu ruled Bobbili; the Pithapuram estate was a separate line.

new.s: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in which century?
new.x: The Bahmani kingdom was founded in 1347, in the 14th century.

new.s: Gulbarga, the first Bahmani capital, was renamed:
new.x: The first Bahmani capital Gulbarga was named Hasanabad.

new.s: Mahmud Gawan, under whom the Bahmani kingdom was largest, was executed in:
new.x: Mahmud Gawan, minister of Muhammad III, was executed in 1481, which broke the kingdom apart.

new.s: Firoz Shah's Bahmani army was beaten at Kambhammetta in 1396 by:
new.x: Kambhammetta (1396) = Gajarao Tippa; Kandukuru (1398) = Machareddi.

new.s: Firoz Shah allied with Pedakomati against which place in 1417?
new.x: Firoz Shah allied with Pedakomati against Rajamahendravaram in 1417.

new.s: Muhammad III and Mahmud Gawan pushed into Odisha in:
new.x: Muhammad III and Mahmud Gawan took Kondaveedu and pushed into Odisha in 1471.

new.s: Which Gajapati ruler refused to help the Bahmani Sultan Muhammad III?
new.x: Purushottama refused to help Muhammad III and recovered ground from the Bahmanis.

new.s: Kapilendra's attack on Tiran Andhra in 1448 is recorded in the:
new.x: The Penugonda inscription records Kapileswara's attack on Tiran Andhra (1448).

new.s: In 1471 the Bahmanis installed which Gajapati prince as their puppet?
new.x: Hamvira was installed as a Bahmani puppet in 1471 and was overturned by Purushottama.

new.s: The capital of the Gajapatis was:
new.x: Gajapati means Lord of Elephants; their capital was Cuttack.

new.s: Rajamahendravaram was taken from the Reddis by Gajapati Kapileswara after:
new.x: Kapileswara took Rajamahendravaram after 1446, after Deva Raya II's death, ending the Rajahmundry Reddis.

new.s: Which Vijayanagara commander helped the Reddis of Rajamahendravaram, as recorded in the Draksharama inscription (1444)?
new.x: The Draksharama inscription (1444) records help from Vijayanagara commander Mallappa Odayar.

new.s: Udayagiri, a major Gajapati stronghold in southern Andhra, is in which present district?
new.x: Udayagiri (Nellore) was the major Gajapati stronghold in southern Andhra.

new.s: Under Gajapati administration, a Dandapata was a:
o: Large province with a standing army
new.x: Dandapata was a large province (whole districts) with a standing army.

new.s: Udayagiri fell to Krishnadevaraya after a siege lasting:
new.x: Udayagiri fell first, after an 18-month siege.

new.s: Krishnadevaraya married Prataparudra Gajapati's daughter:
new.x: Prataparudra's daughter Annapurna Devi (also Bhadradevi/Tukkadevi/Jaganmohini) married Krishnadevaraya.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Krishnadevaraya–Prataparudra peace:
1. Lands north of the Krishna were returned to the Gajapati.
2. Cuttack was annexed to Vijayanagara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Lands north of the Krishna were returned and the Gajapati stayed a feudatory; Cuttack was not taken over.

new.s: The Raichur Doab lies between the rivers:
new.x: The Raichur Doab lies between the Krishna and Tungabhadra; Rajahmundry and Kondaveedu lie in the Krishna–Godavari region.

new.s: In the Battle of Raichur (1520), Krishnadevaraya defeated:
new.x: In the Battle of Raichur (1520) Krishnadevaraya beat Bijapur.

new.s: The rivalry over the Krishna–Godavari region of coastal Andhra was mainly among:
new.x: Coastal Andhra (Krishna–Godavari) was contested by the Gajapatis, Vijayanagara and the Bahmanis; the Raichur Doab was Bahmani vs Vijayanagara.

new.s: Krishnadevaraya's victory pillars over the Gajapatis stand at:
new.x: The victory pillars at Simhachalam and Potnuru mark Krishnadevaraya's triumph over the Gajapatis.

new.s: The Anantavaram inscription of Prataparudra records that the Virupaksharayas were made to pay:
new.x: The Anantavaram inscription says the Virupaksharayas were defeated and made to pay Kappam.

new.s: The sister languages of Telugu in the South-Central Dravidian sub-branch include:
new.x: Telugu is South-Central Dravidian with Gondi and Kui; Tamil and Malayalam are South Dravidian.

new.s: The second official language of Andhra Pradesh is:
new.x: Telugu is the official language of AP; Urdu is the second official language.

new.s: Who first used the words 'Tenugu' and 'Telugu'?
new.x: Ketana first used the words Tenugu/Telugu.

new.s: Niccolo de' Conti called Telugu the 'Italian of the East' because its words:
new.x: Conti, a 15th-century Venetian traveller, compared Telugu to Italian because its words end in vowels.

new.s: Telugu Language Day, 29 August, marks the birth anniversary of:
new.x: 29 August is Gidugu Venkata Ramamurthy's birth anniversary, not Gurajada's.

new.s: The Telugu word 'Vepuru' occurs in which inscription?
new.x: 'Vepuru' is from the Myakadoni inscription; 'Nagabu' from Amaravati.

new.s: The Telugu plural form '-ambul' appears in the Chikkulla plates of the:
new.x: The Chikkulla plates of the Vishnukundins use the plural '-ambul' (Vijayarajya Samvatsarambul).

new.s: In the early medieval (Kadamba–Chalukya) period, Telugu was written in:
new.x: In the Kadamba–Chalukya period a common Old Kannada–Telugu script was used; the separate Telugu script came in the 11th–14th centuries.

new.s: The Vipparla inscription was issued by:
new.x: Vipparla is Jayasimha Vallabha I's (G2 2017 key); Chejarla is Kubja Vishnuvardhana's.

new.s: The Chejarla inscription, with over 50% Telugu words, belongs to:
new.x: Chejarla is Kubja Vishnuvardhana's inscription with over 50% Telugu words.

new.s: The Kalamalla inscription, the first Telugu inscription, is dated to about:
new.x: Kalamalla (Kadapa), by Renati Chola Erikal Mutturaju Dhananjaya, dates to c. 575 CE.

new.s: The first poetic inscription in Telugu, at Addanki, is in which metre?
new.x: Addanki is the first poetic inscription, in Taruvoja; Bezawada has the first Madhyakkara.

new.s: The Bezawada inscription with the first Madhyakkara poem was issued by:
new.x: The Bezawada (Nagamalleswara temple) inscription is Yuddhamalla II's.

new.s: The Kandukur inscription of Gunaga Vijayaditya uses which metre?
new.x: Kandukur and Dharmavaram use Seesa and Ataveladi.

new.s: In bilingual Eastern Chalukya records, the grant details were written in:
new.x: Eastern Chalukya records gave the praise in Sanskrit and the grant details in Telugu.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT a pre-Nannaya record of written Telugu?
new.x: Motupalli is a later Kakatiya record; Kalamalla, Vipparla, Addanki and Bezawada are pre-Nannaya.

new.s: Errana, the last of the Kavitrayam, belonged to which century?
new.x: Nannaya – 11th, Tikkana – 13th, Errana – 14th century.

new.s: The title 'Prabandha Parameswara' belonged to:
new.x: Errana held the titles Prabandha Parameswara and Sambhudasa.

new.s: Rajaraja Narendra, Nannaya's patron, ruled from:
new.x: Rajaraja Narendra (r. 1018–1061), Eastern Chalukya, ruled from Rajamahendravaram.

new.s: Tikkana translated the parvas of the Mahabharata from:
new.x: Tikkana translated the remaining 15 parvas, Virata to Swargarohana.

new.s: Which of the following is a title of Nannaya?
new.x: Nannaya's titles include Adikavi, Vagadheeshwara and Shabda Shasanudu; Kavibrahma is Tikkana's.

new.s: Nannaya pioneered which form of writing that mixes prose and verse?
new.x: Nannaya pioneered the Champu style of prose with verse.

new.s: Narayana Bhattu was made his representative at Rajamahendravaram by:
new.x: Someshwara I of Kalyani made Narayana Bhattu his representative at Rajamahendravaram.

new.s: Kavi Vakbandham is a work of:
new.x: Tikkana wrote Kavi Vakbandham and Krishna Satakam besides his Bharatam.

new.s: Errana dedicated his Harivamsam to:
new.x: Errana's Harivamsam was dedicated to Prolaya Vema Reddi.

new.s: Sivatattvasaram, of about 400 kanda poems, was written by:
new.x: Mallikarjuna Panditaradhya wrote Sivatattvasaram and originated the Sataka form.

new.s: Panditaradhya Charitra, called the first Telugu encyclopaedia, was written by:
new.x: Palkuriki Somanatha wrote Basava Puranam, Panditaradhya Charitra and Vrushadhipa Satakam.

new.s: Palkuriki Somanatha's Basava Puranam deals with:
new.x: Basava Puranam narrates the life of Basava and Veerashaivism.

new.s: Sumathi Satakam was written by:
new.x: Baddena wrote Sumathi Satakam and Nitisastra Muktavali.

new.s: Manchana's Keyurabahu Charitra is based on Rajasekhara's:
new.x: Keyurabahu Charitra is from Rajasekhara's Viddhasalabhanjika.

new.s: Ranganatha Ramayanam of Gona Budda Reddy is also the first Telugu kavya in:
new.x: Ranganatha Ramayanam is the first Telugu Ramayana and the first dwipada kavya.

new.s: Kavyalankara Chudamani, the first alankara work in Telugu, was written by:
new.x: Kavyalankara Chudamani is by Vinnakota Peddana; Kavijanasrayam is by Malliya Rechana.

new.s: Appakaviyam, a Telugu grammar of the 17th century, was written by:
new.x: Appakaviyam is by Kakunuri Appakavi (17th c.); Appayacharya wrote Jinendra Kalyanabhyudayamu.

new.s: Kreedabhiramam describes life in which city?
new.x: Kreedabhiramam describes Orugallu (Warangal) – its markets, nightlife and Kakati Devi temple.

new.s: Kreedabhiramam is attributed to:
new.x: Kreedabhiramam is by Vinukonda Vallabharaya, a Telugu rendering of Tripurantakudu's Premabhiramam.

new.s: Vidyanatha was the court poet of Kakatiya:
new.x: Vidyanatha, author of Prataparudra Yashobhushanam, was court poet of Prataparudra II.

new.s: The first Yakshagana in Telugu, Sugriva Vijayam, was written by:
new.x: Sugriva Vijayam by Kandukuri Rudrakavi is the first Yakshagana.

new.s: Raghavapandaviyam of Pingali Surana is the first example of which form?
new.x: Raghavapandaviyam tells the Ramayana and Mahabharata at once – a dvyarthi kavya.

new.s: The Shiva Kavi Yugam of Telugu literature is dated:
new.x: The Shiva Kavi Yugam is dated 1060–1260.

new.s: Which work is called the first champu kavya in Telugu (one claim)?
new.x: Hulakki Bhaskara's Bhaskara Ramayanam is called the first champu kavya.

new.s: Srinatha's Haravilasam was dedicated to the merchant:
new.x: Haravilasam was dedicated to merchant Tippayya Setti; Kashikhandam was at Kataya Vema's request.

new.s: Srinatha received the title 'Kavisarvabhauma' from:
new.x: Deva Raya II gave Srinatha the title Kavisarvabhauma.

new.s: Srinatha's Sringara Naishadham tells the story of:
new.x: Sringara Naishadham, from Sriharsha's Naishadhiyacharita, is about Nala and Damayanti.

new.s: The Telugu Prabandha reached its peak with the:
new.x: The prabandha reached its peak with the Ashtadiggajas of Vijayanagara.

new.s: Pampa's Vikramarjuna Vijaya is a Mahabharata in:
new.x: Pampa's Vikramarjuna Vijaya (Pampa Bharata) is in Kannada.

new.s: Kasirama Das composed the Mahabharata in:
new.x: Kasirama Das wrote the Bengali Mahabharata; Sarala Dasa's is Odia.

new.s: Kamban received the title 'Kavi Chakravarti' from:
new.x: Kamban (Ramavataram, Tamil, 12th c.) got the title Kavi Chakravarti from Kulottunga III.

new.s: Tyagaraja's kritis on Rama are in which language?
new.x: Tyagaraja lived at Thanjavur but composed his kritis in Telugu.

new.s: Manucharitra was written by:
new.x: Manucharitra is by Allasani Peddana, the Andhra Kavita Pitamaha.

new.s: The title 'Andhra Kavita Pitamaha' belongs to:
new.x: Andhra Kavita Pitamaha = Allasani Peddana; Kavibrahma = Tikkana.

new.s: Kalahastiswara Satakam was written by:
new.x: Kalahastiswara Satakam is by Dhurjati.

new.s: Which of the following pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: The Vilasa grant (1330) is Prolaya Nayaka's; the Kaluvacheru grant (1423) is Anitalli's.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correctly matched with Kapaya Nayaka's losses to the Bahmanis?
new.x: Bhuvanagiri was lost in 1356; in 1347 Kapaya helped Hasan Gangu found the Bahmani kingdom.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Anapota Nayaka:
1. He was the son of Singama Nayaka I.
2. He shifted the capital from Amanagallu to Rachakonda.
3. He moved the Reddi capital from Addanki to Kondaveedu.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Anapota Nayaka (Velama), Singama's son, moved the capital to Rachakonda; it was Anapota Reddi who moved the Reddi capital to Kondaveedu.

new.s: Which of the following battle–outcome pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Singama died at Jallipalli; Kapaya was killed at Bhimavaram; the Velamas won at Dharanikota.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about the Velamas' foreign relations:
1. Deva Raya I of Vijayanagara allied with them.
2. Mahmud Gawan crushed the Telangana revolts with their help.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Deva Raya I allied with the Velamas, and Mahmud Gawan used Velama help against the Telangana revolts.

new.s: Which of the following dynasty–capital pairs is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: The Reddi capitals were Addanki, Kondaveedu and Rajahmundry; Devarakonda was a Recherla capital.

new.s: Which of the following Bahmani incursion–opponent pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Kandukuru (1398) = Machareddi; Kambhammetta (1396) = Gajarao Tippa.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Kapilendra Gajapati:
1. He founded the Gajapati line.
2. He took Kondaveedu around 1450.
3. He lost Udayagiri to Krishnadevaraya.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Kapilendra founded the line and took Kondaveedu c. 1450; Udayagiri was lost by Prataparudra.

new.s: Which of the following is NOT correct about Gajapati administration in Andhra?
o: Naidu was a revenue officer in southern Andhra
A Dandapata was a large province with a standing army
The Reddi-era social order was abolished
new.x: The Reddi-era social order was kept under the Gajapatis.

new.s: Which of the following record–content pairs is correctly matched?
o: Penugonda inscription – attack on Tiran Andhra (1448)
Draksharama inscription – attack on Tiran Andhra (1448)
Anantavaram inscription – Vijayanagara help to the Reddis
Penugonda inscription – Vijayanagara help to the Reddis
new.x: Penugonda records Kapileswara's attack on Tiran Andhra; Draksharama (1444) records Vijayanagara help to the Reddis.

new.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. 'Italian of the East' was coined by Niccolo de' Conti.
2. 'Desa bhashalandu Telugu lessa' occurs in Amuktamalyada.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Conti, a Venetian traveller, coined the epithet; Krishnadevaraya wrote the line in Amuktamalyada.

new.s: Which of the following inscription–metre pairs is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Addanki is in Taruvoja; the first Madhyakkara is in the Bezawada inscription.

new.s: Which of the following poet–title pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Errana = Sambhudasa; Nannaya = Adikavi; Tikkana = Kavibrahma; Srinatha = Kavisarvabhauma.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Palkuriki Somanatha:
1. He led the Desi kavita movement.
2. He popularised the dwipada.
3. He wrote Kumarasambhavam.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Palkuriki led the Desi kavita movement and popularised dwipada; Kumarasambhavam is Nannechoda's.

new.s:
Consider the following statements about Pavuluri Mallana:
1. He wrote the first Telugu mathematics book.
2. He received the Navakhandavada agrahara.
Which of the statements given above is/are correct?
new.x: Both are correct: Pavuluri Mallana wrote Sara Sangraha Ganitam and received Navakhandavada from Rajaraja Narendra.

new.s: Which of the following works is NOT by Srinatha?
new.x: Veerabhadra Vijayam is by Bammera Potana.

new.s: Which of the following composer–language pairs is NOT correctly matched?
new.x: Sarala Dasa composed the Mahabharata in Odia; Kasirama Das's is Bengali.

new.s: Which of the following poet–language pairs is correctly matched?
new.x: Eknath wrote in Marathi; Waris Shah in Punjabi, Kunchan Nambiar in Malayalam, Dayaram in Gujarati.
